title: A demand shock

controls.label: AD shift (billions at every price level)

predict.q: The economy starts in long-run equilibrium. Confidence collapses and AD shifts left. What happens in the short run?

options.s: Price level falls, real output falls
options.fb: The economy moves down along SRAS: e.g. AD −125 gives price level 105 and output 1,925, a gap of −3.75%.

options.s: Price level rises, real output falls
options.fb: Prices rise when output falls is a supply-shock pattern. A fall in AD moves the economy down along SRAS, so the price level falls too.

options.s: Price level falls, real output stays at full employment
options.fb: LRAS limits output only in the long run. In the short run, the economy moves along SRAS, so output falls below potential.

task: Move the AD slider left, then right, and watch the price level, real output and unemployment.

target.do: Move the AD slider to the left, then press Check.

takeaway: AD shocks move the price level and real output in the same direction.
